author: root controlled probe + read-only reconciliation
scope: One controlled owned-state replacement failure and subsequent same-session fast reconnect. This is not whole-Goal or system reliability acceptance.

observed.injector_exit_reason: Conservative additional-temp guard released reader and exited when following recovery-state temp appeared. No second injection; this reconciliation reads lifecycle metadata only.

evidence: Intent binds the existing Goal, original session/spec hash, runner source hash, controller PID+creation token, original owner token, and live coding-worker process token. The current deployed runner hash still matches the probe intent and reconciled result.

The scoped event slice begins at the recorded intent offset: recovery event is OwnedSnapshotUnavailable, then infrastructure_reconnect, owner process start, initialization with the same native session, and required-tools-ready. No supervisor process start or session_reset appeared in the slice.
Reader receipt confirms the first controller-owned temp was observed and the read handle closed. It held for about 25.45 seconds, below the 30-second no-op release and 3-second post-temp guard.

Read-only current identity checks confirm controller PID/token unchanged, original owner identity absent, coding worker identity still live, and the replacement owner identity live. Current Goal state retains the same session and spec and remains RUNNING.

The injector exited 1 after its conservative additional-temp guard saw a subsequent recovery-state temp. It did not reinject. A separate read-only reconciliation captured the completed recovery chain and reports all 13 acceptance predicates true.
limitations: This proves one controlled fault/recovery instance only. The Goal is still RUNNING; no Goal completion or broader reliability claim is made.
No product/source-C files, native capture, or live actions were performed during this review.
